priorStories.headline: Hurricane Polo reaches Category 4 off Mexico
priorStories.body:
Hurricane Polo rapidly strengthened into a Category 4 storm late Monday, with maximum sustained winds of 130 mph, according to the U.S. National Hurricane Center.

The storm remained offshore, but forecasters warned of heavy rain, flooding, mudslides and hazardous seas in southwestern Mexico. Further strengthening was possible.

priorStories.headline: Pennsylvania measles outbreak reaches 792 cases
priorStories.body:
The Pennsylvania Department of Health reported 792 measles cases, 25 more than on September 18, and 155 hospitalizations. Lancaster County remained the hardest-hit area.

Reuters described the state outbreak as part of the largest U.S. measles resurgence in decades.

priorStories.headline: United Russia retains constitutional majority
priorStories.body:
Russia’s Central Election Commission said United Russia received 57.83% of the party-list vote with more than 95% of ballots counted. The preliminary result would give the ruling party 355 of the State Duma’s 450 seats, preserving its constitutional majority.

The election took place under tight political controls. Voting was also conducted in Russian-controlled parts of Ukraine, which Kyiv and Western governments consider illegally occupied.

priorStories.headline: Texas pauses data-center permits for audits
priorStories.body:
Texas Governor Greg Abbott directed the state environmental agency to stop issuing permits sought by data centers until grid and water regulators complete audits of the facilities.

The directive pauses state regulatory approvals; it does not permanently prohibit data-center development.

priorStories.headline: Fighting displaces more than 129,000 in Yemen
priorStories.body:
Renewed fighting in Yemen has displaced 129,438 people across seven provinces, according to the International Organization for Migration. That includes 11,352 people displaced during the three days beginning September 18.

The World Food Programme said it had provided meals or food supplies to about 60,000 people and was building stocks to assist hundreds of thousands more. The United Nations has reported nearly 700 deaths in the escalation.

candidates.summary: Gunmen killed two police officers assigned to protect polio vaccination workers during a door-to-door campaign in southwestern Pakistan, officials said. The attack occurred as Pakistan continued efforts to interrupt transmission of wild poliovirus.
candidates.title: Two police guarding polio workers killed in Pakistan

candidates.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump signed an agreement with Denmark and Greenland intended to strengthen Arctic and North Atlantic security. The agreement, signed on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, followed tensions over Trump's calls for Greenland to become part of the United States.
candidates.title: US, Denmark and Greenland sign Arctic security agreement

candidates.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump defended his decision to begin the war against Iran in an address to the United Nations General Assembly. He said the United States could reach an agreement with Iran but again threatened the country's government if no deal was reached.
candidates.title: Trump defends Iran war in UN address
